Heat exhaustion and heat stroke in kids can happen quickly during fall sports.
Football, soccer, baseball and other fall sports may feel like a return to routine, but hot weather can remain a serious concern. The American Academy of Pediatrics says a heat index of 90°F or higher can be dangerous, particularly for young children and kids participating in sports.
Young athletes can be especially vulnerable when exercising in high heat and humidity. The AAP warns that these conditions can cause heat illness "even [in] well-trained athletes," while Children's Health notes that intense practices and camps during the hottest parts of the day increase athletes' risk.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Kids may also fail to recognize that they're becoming overheated. Pediatric sports medicine physician Troy Smurawa says, "It's very important for parents, kids and athletes to be mindful of the heat," because children don't always recognize the effects of heat until they're already in trouble.
Heat Exhaustion or Heat Stroke? Know the Difference
Heat exhaustion often develops after exercise or play in the heat, particularly when a child becomes dehydrated from losing fluids and salt through sweating. Symptoms can include increased thirst, weakness, dizziness, headache, nausea, muscle cramps, heavy sweating and cool, clammy skin.
Heat stroke is considerably more dangerous and requires immediate emergency medical attention. Nemours KidsHealth defines heat stroke as occurring when body temperature reaches 105°F (40.5°C) or higher, with symptoms potentially including confusion, loss of consciousness, seizures, rapid breathing and heartbeat, and little or no sweating.
The distinction matters because heat exhaustion can progress to heat stroke if it isn't treated promptly. Children's Health warns that heat stroke can cause brain damage or death if it isn't treated quickly.
5 Ways Parents Can Help Kids Beat the Heat
1. Hydrate before the whistle blows. Kids should drink plenty of fluids before and during activity, even if they aren't thirsty, according to Nemours KidsHealth.
Advertisement
Advertisement
2. Build in breaks. Parents should ask coaches about regular water and rest breaks, while the AAP recommends frequent breaks and scheduling strenuous activities during cooler parts of the day when possible.

- RBI push: Forex reserves at all-time high of $729.3bn
Trending
MUMBAI: The country’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $12.4 billion in the week ended Aug 21, to an all-time high of $729.3 billion, driven largely by non-resident deposits drawn through a special scheme under which RBI took over the foreign currency risks from banks. Foreign currency assets, the largest component, rose $9.5 billion to $591.3 billion, while gold reserves increased $2.8 billion to $114.2 billion.
The previous record was $728.5 billion on Feb 27, 2026, just before the outbreak of the US-Iran war. Higher crude oil prices and pressure on the rupee subsequently prompted RBI intervention, taking reserves to a low of $666.9 billion on June 26.The largest weekly increase in total reserves was recorded in the week ended Aug 27, 2021, when reserves rose sharply following a major allocation of special drawing rights by the IMF.For the financial year so far, total reserves have increased by $38.2 billion from end-March 2026. FCA have risen $39.1 billion, more than the overall increase, while gold reserves have declined $1.2 billion.The recent rise in reserves, particularly FCA, has been supported by RBI measures to attract dollar inflows and manage rupee volatility. In June, RBI and govt launched a concessional USD-INR forex swap facility for FCNR(B) deposits, overseas foreign currency borrowings and ECBs.The facility has mobilised an estimated $65 billion to $73 billion ahead of its Aug 31 closure.

articles.full_text:
Rainfall activity is set to intensify across Odisha as a fresh low-pressure area is likely to develop over the northwest Bay of Bengal on Saturday, August 29, under the influence of a cyclonic circulation.
The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Bhubaneswar, has issued an orange warning for six districts, forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall. A yellow warning has also been issued for 24 districts as several parts of the state may experience thunderstorms accompanied by lightning.
The weather system is expected to bring an increase in rainfall activity from August 30, with many areas likely to witness thunderstorms over the next four days.
Six districts under orange warning
According to RMC Director Manorama Mohanty, several districts are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall as the weather system develops.
Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, Balasore, Bhadrak, Kendrapara and Jagatsinghpur are among the districts expected to experience intense rainfall.
“Various places across the state are likely to receive light to moderate rainfall. Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, Balasore, Bhadrak, Kendrapara and Jagatsinghpur districts are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall,” Mohanty said.
The forecast comes amid heightened monsoon activity over Odisha and adjoining areas of the Bay of Bengal.
Heavy rain forecast in several other districts
Apart from the districts under the orange warning, heavy rainfall is also likely at some places in Puri, Khordha, Nayagarh, Jajpur, Angul, Dhenkanal, Sundargarh, Sambalpur, Deogarh, Bargarh, Nuapada, Bolangir, Nabarangpur, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Boudh and Sonepur.
Several areas may also experience thunderstorms and lightning during the period.
With the low-pressure area expected to become more influential from Sunday, rainfall activity could increase further across different parts of the state.
Residents advised to remain cautious
Authorities have urged people, particularly those living in districts under the orange warning, to remain alert and take necessary precautions.
Residents have also been advised to exercise caution during thunderstorms and lightning and stay updated with official weather advisories.
The developing system over the Bay of Bengal is expected to keep Odisha’s weather unsettled over the coming days, with periods of heavy rainfall likely in several districts.

MANILA, Philippines — The government is on "red alert" in anticipation of the effects of the persistent monsoon rains in parts of the country, including Metro Manila.
The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), the lead agencies in disaster response, are monitoring the situation in areas where heavy rainfall is expected based on the forecast by the Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) early Saturday.
In an advisory, Pagasa said that moderate to heavy monsoon rains are expected over Ilocos Sur, Benguet, La Union, Pangasinan, Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac and Pampanga. while occasional rains are expected in Metro Manila, Ilocos Norte, Abra, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Ecija, Nueva Vizcaya, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, Laguna, Oriental Mindoro and Occidental Mindoro.
DSWD Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao said that the department's field offices were ready for possible deployment.
"We remain prepared as we know that the effects of the southwest monsoon continue to persist in parts of Luzon and the Visayas," Dumlao said in Filipino.

The NDRRMC went on red alert on Friday.
Meanwhile, 12 local governments units (LGUs) in Metro Manila suspended face-to-face (F2F) classes in both public and private schools on Saturday, the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) said.
The affected cities are Caloocan, Valenzuela, Manila, Navotas, Marikina, Malabon, Las Piñas, Mandaluyong, Taguig, Pasay, Muntinlupa and San Juan.
Caloocan, Valenzuela, Las Piñas and Marikina suspended face-to-face classes for all levels in public and private schools. Marikina also suspended online classes.

Manila, Navotas, Malabon and Mandaluyong suspended face-to-face classes for all levels and shifted to alternative learning or delivery modes.
Taguig and Pasay shifted to alternative learning modalities, while Muntinlupa suspended face-to-face classes for all levels, including the Alternative Learning System, Early Childhood Education Division and Muntinlupa City Technical Institute.
San Juan also suspended face-to-face classes for all levels and shifted to alternative learning modalities.
The MMDA advised the public to check for updates on class suspensions, and may call its 136 hotline for assistance.
Advertisement
Aside from the monsoon rains, Pagasa is also monitoring two low pressure areas, with one inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) but with a low chance of developing into a tropical cyclone within the next 24 hours.
The other LPA, outside the PAR has a moderate chance of developing into a tropical cyclone and could enter PAR this weekend.

Dutch issues ‘Red Alert’ over lethal Trump-Shaped Ecstasy Pills
August 29, 2026 at
3:48 PM
Dutch authorities have issued a “red alert” over potentially lethal ecstasy pills shaped like US President Donald Trump’s head.
The Trimbos Institute said several pills submitted for testing in August contained “very high” levels of PMMA, a substance similar to MDMA that can cause dangerous overheating and potentially fatal consequences.
“Do not use this pill under any circumstance,” the institute warned.
The pills feature Trump’s face on one side, with “Trump” and “NL” stamped on the other. No deaths or serious illnesses linked to the pills have been reported so far, according to the institute. (Newswire)
